title.narrative: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Revenue Mobilization and Public Resource Management

description.narrative: The development objective of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) Revenue Mobilization and Public Resource Management Project for Pakistan is to increase the collection of KP's own source revenues (OSR) and improve the management of public Resources. The Government of KP (GoKP's) public financial management reform strategy (PFMRS) covers the whole PFM cycle at the provincial and local government (LG) levels. The strategy is organized around six objectives: (a) ensuring policy-driven planning and budgeting; (b) facilitating a comprehensive, credible, and transparent annual budget; (c) improving predictability and control in budget execution; (d) enabling resource mobilization and enhancing provincial OSR; (e) improving asset and liability management; and (f) fostering accountability for results. The program is divided into two parts: part one, program-for-results and part two, investment project financing.
To increase the collection of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's own source revenues and improve the management of public resources

Replacement of vehicle registration books with PVC cards is in process. 2. The department is testing the digitization of property tax demand notice in selected districts. 3. KP Revenue Authority has completed portal for registration and deregistration of taxpayers. Online filing of sales tax returns (through national single portal), payment of taxes, and tax notice are also digitized. 4. Board of Revenue has completed process improvement for land registration, land mutations, land title document (fard) issuance and stamp fee collections. target.value: 12 TFCs

comment.narrative: A study has been completed to inform the design of joint Taxpayer Facilitation Centers (TFCs) in KP. While the tax authorities have separate facilitation counters in their main/field offices. KPITB is working on a plan to establish Citizen Facilitation Centers (CFC) where various public services, including tax related services, will be provided at one place. In this regard, KP Government signed MOU with NESPAK and NADRA to operationalize 7 CFCs at divisional level (Peshawar, Mardan, Abbottabad, Kohat, D.I.Khan, Bannu, and Swat). The CFCs in Swat and Bannu are ready for inauguration, while remaining CFCs are being renovated. The CFC portal has 19 online services (including for excise & taxation department and BOR). The system needs to be reviewed from the perspective of services for taxpayers.

actual.value: 12 TFCs not established

title.narrative: Increase in own source tax revenues (USD million)

comment.narrative:
Revision: Considering improved performance of KP Government in revenue mobilization, OSR targets included for extended period of Program (5% increase each year), using FY24 as baseline (USD 202mn).
As per revised estimates, KP collected tax revenues of Rs. 56 billion from own sources in FY24. Around 57% of tax revenue was collected from Sales Tax, whereas 25% of tax revenue was collected from land revenue, stamp duty, property tax, and motor vehicle tax. Final audited numbers for tax revenue collection will be available by June 2025. The provinceâ€™s tax collections upto February 2025 was Rs. 36 billion or USD 129 million, against the target of USD 212 million. The provisional numbers for own source tax collections during FY25 will be available by June 2025.
